experiment: EM1 — emergence at the level of one simple tissue unit: a single hair bundle built from its molecular elements
principle: Author: complex structures cannot be emerged realistically (environment cannot be matched), but simple tissues emerge accurately. Elements and constants are observations; the bundle's behaviour is NOT set, it must emerge. No constant is tuned to the outputs.
model: Nadrowski, Martin & Juelicher 2004 (PNAS 101:12195) two-variable bundle: gating springs + transduction channels (open probability from gating), adaptation motors (myosin) with Ca feedback on motor force. Deterministic (no noise term).
control_parameter: F_max (motor force) scanned 20-90 pN; the reported 50.3 pN is evaluated as is

observations_to_compare.O1: bullfrog saccular bundles oscillate spontaneously at ~5-50 Hz with ~20-80 nm amplitude (Martin & Hudspeth 2001; Martin, Bozovic et al. 2003)
observations_to_compare.O2: near their characteristic frequency, bundle displacement grows as the 1/3 power of the stimulus force over a range of forces (Martin & Hudspeth 2001, PNAS 98:14386)
observations_to_compare.O3: cochlear basilar-membrane compression is ~0.2 dB/dB (Ruggero 1997) — a whole-organ (complex-structure) observation

predictions.P1_hopf_emerges: a finite F_max window produces self-sustained oscillation (not put in by hand); the reported 50.3 pN lies inside it
predictions.P2_frequency_amplitude: at 50.3 pN the emergent oscillation has frequency 5-50 Hz and peak-to-peak amplitude 20-150 nm
predictions.P3_compression: just on the quiescent side of the emergent bifurcation, the response at the characteristic frequency grows with force with a local exponent between 0.25 and 0.45 over some force decade
predictions.P4_organ_gap: the single-bundle exponent does not go below 0.25 in the compressive range, i.e. the organ-level 0.2 is NOT produced by one bundle (a complex-structure effect, left [O])
